art: A risograph screen-print: exactly two flat inks — federal blue and fluorescent pink — on warm off-white stock, halftone dot fields instead of gradients, a deliberate slight misregistration between the two passes, bold simple shapes. Hand-printed and charmingly imperfect.
mood: A risograph-printed zine: warm off-white stock printed in exactly two inks — federal blue and fluorescent pink — with the charming imperfection of the medium. Body text is the blue ink (--ink is a deep blue, not black); pink is the shout. Signatures to reproduce structurally: (1) headings carry a slight misregistration — a pink duplicate of the heading offset 2–3px behind the blue via text-shadow or a pseudo-element, as if the second ink pass drifted; (2) emphasis blocks are solid pink or blue panels with the paper color knocked out as the text; (3) images and diagrams should look screen-printed: flat two-color fills, halftone-dot patterns (radial-gradient dots) instead of photographic gradients; (4) section dividers are chunky hand-drawn-feeling bars or stars, never hairlines. Corners slightly rounded, edges a little imperfect. The feel: a smart friend's hand-made pamphlet about a serious topic — punchy, warm, unafraid of ink.
name: Riso
tagline: Two-ink zine — federal blue + fluoro pink, lovingly misregistered
